summary: The ordered trace resolves the ambiguity in the clean-miss construction: `decide7:2-2>2-2|prepare:2-2>2-2|accsync1:2-2>3-3`. Node 5 received only one Decide (sequence counter 7), its indices did not change, then a Prepare and an AcceptSync moved it to accepted 3 and decided 3. Since the leader only sends Prepare for a not-promised peer or in response to a PrepareReq, the Decide must have been rejected as a sequence break rather than processed, so the follower reconnected and the AcceptSync repaired it. That withdraws the strong 'no enabled repair' claim for a straight AcceptStopSign loss and means the run-13 stall needs a different explanation. This experiment therefore leaves the seeded 900-action lossy run, reconfigure at action 450, 150-round fair-delivery convergence, existing fields and the converged_all comparison unchanged, and adds a bounded ordered trace of the Paxos messages delivered to the actual lagging node 3 (kind, sequence counter, accepted/decided before and after) plus counts of the PrepareReq and Promise messages node 3 sends during convergence. The receipt should show whether node 3 receives any Decide at all after the StopSign decision, whether it ever detects a sequence break, and whether anything carries the missing StopSign to it.
